title: Caring for cotton crochet
subtitle: How to wash, dry, and press crochet made from cotton yarn
excerpt: Cotton is durable and machine-washable but it can shrink in hot water and will wrinkle if dried in a heap. Handled correctly it gets better with washing rather than worse.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book. Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins).

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of wetting or steaming a finished piece and shaping it to measurements while damp or under heat, so it dries or cools in the correct dimensions.

content.text: Cotton yarn is one of the most durable crochet fibres. It does not felt, it withstands repeated washing, and it softens slightly over time. The main risks are shrinkage from hot water and colour bleeding on first wash. Both are easy to avoid with the right approach.

Most cotton yarn is machine-washable. Wash at 30 degrees C or 40 degrees C to avoid shrinkage. Check the ball band; some cotton blends need a lower temperature. Use a gentle cycle and a mesh laundry bag for smaller pieces or items with fine stitch detail.

Deeply dyed cotton can bleed dye on the first wash. Before washing a finished piece with other items, wash it alone or with a colour-catcher sheet. If the water runs strongly coloured, rinse until it runs clear before the final wash.
Cotton can be tumble-dried on a low heat, but it may shrink slightly. Laying flat to dry gives more control over the final shape. For items that are
to exact measurements (placemats, blanket squares), lay flat every time.

Cotton crochet can be pressed with a steam iron to remove creases and improve stitch definition. Use a pressing cloth between the iron and the fabric for fine stitch patterns. Cotton handles higher heat than wool or acrylic, but keep the iron moving to avoid over-heating.

items.symptom: The cotton piece shrank noticeably on first wash
items.cause: It was washed at too high a temperature.
items.fix: Future washes should be at 30 degrees C. For the current piece, rewash at 30 degrees C and block to the correct measurements while still damp.

items.symptom: The colour transferred to other items in the wash
items.cause: The cotton dye was not fixed before the first wash.
items.fix: Wash the affected items again with a colour-catcher. Next time, wash new cotton yarn on its own for the first wash.

content.text: If you are making something that will be washed frequently (dishcloths, market bags, baby bibs), pre-wash the yarn before starting the project. This removes any excess dye and means the finished piece will not shrink the first time it is used.
